14	CASE OD2-HO-STOP-1 (STOP, organizational): The August dip at Calder Quay Hotel

I've read a handful of the August comments and one on a booking site called the room 'tired and dusty'. Complaints logged at the desk are up roughly 40%. My view is that Orrin is the problem and we should serve notice before the 1 October renewal window closes. Please also tell me whether we need to pull the kiosks. I want a recommendation by Friday.

Floors 6-8 (84 rooms; 157 August responses): overall 8.6 to 7.4; room comfort 8.4 to 6.1; cleanliness 8.7 to 8.6; check-in 8.8 to 8.7; value for money 8.0 to 7.3. Vendor note: for this property, month-to-month movements under 0.2 on any score fall within normal variation (trailing 18 months).
20	E3 [stage S1] Engineering work-order log, WO-26-0814 (log): 04 Aug 15:20 | Chiller CH-2 (east riser, serves floors 6-8) tripped on compressor fault. Reset failed. Guest calls about heat: 23 by 21:00. 05 Aug 09:40 | Contractor diagnosis: failed compressor contactor. Part not in stock; supplier lead time 11 working days. Portable units deployed to 12 rooms (all held). 07-18 Aug | Spot readings in occupied rooms on floors 6-8: 26.5-29.0 C (set point 22). 19 Aug 14:10 | Contactor fitted, CH-2 restored. Floors 6-8 below 23 C by 22:00. Notes: annual preventive maintenance on both CH-2 and CH-1 (west riser, floors 1-5) deferred in April 2026 under a budget hold; neither yet rescheduled. CH-1 has not faulted this year.
21	E4 [stage S1] Pellmore Insights daily view and verbatim tagging report, August 2026 (system-record): Floors 6-8 overall score by checkout date: 1-4 Aug 8.5 (n=19); 5-20 Aug 6.8 (n=96); 21-31 Aug 8.4 (n=42); 1-14 Sep 8.6 (n=71). Floors 1-5 daily scores stayed between 8.4 and 8.6 throughout August and early September. Verbatim tagging, August (vendor auto-tags, spot-checked by guest relations): 74 negative comments, 61 of them from floors 6-8. Heat / air conditioning / 'stuffy': 56, all floors 6-8. Cleanliness: 4 (July: 5), 2 per block. Check-in or kiosk: 2 (July: 3). Price or value: 6 (July: 2), 4 of them from floors 1-5. Other: 6.
22	E5 [stage S1] Rooms division monthly KPI pack, compiled by the Executive Housekeeper and Front Office Manager (system-record): Room inspections are done by in-house supervisors, not by the contractor. Pass rate: June 95% (Linthwaite, prior contractor); July 96% (Orrin); August 95% (Orrin), with 95% on floors 1-5 and 95% on floors 6-8. About 640 inspections a month. Front-desk complaint log: July 50 entries, August 71. August by category (July in brackets): room temperature 24 (1); noise 11 (12); housekeeping 9 (10); billing 8 (9); kiosk/check-in 6 (7); other 13 (11). Share of guests checking in at kiosks: July 41%, August 43%. Average queue at peak: July 4.1 min, August 3.9 min. Outage recovery: all 517 floor 6-8 stays checking out 5-20 August received a written apology and a goodwill credit of half a night's rate at checkout.
23	E6 [stage S1] Note from Priya Vantongeren, Revenue Manager, to the General Manager, 3 September 2026 (manager-account): 'Rack and BAR rates went up 6% hotel-wide from 1 August, as planned in the annual budget. We review rates weekly and can move them at any time. I can't tell you whether that hurt the value score. Value for money dips every August here: last year it went from 8.1 to 7.9 with no rate change, because of festival-season pricing across the city, and the overall score went from 8.5 to 8.4 last August as well. This year's value drop on floors 1-5 is slightly bigger, but nothing I have separates the rate rise from the usual seasonal dip.'
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Orrin Facility Group monthly service reports, July-August 2026 - Orrin Facility Group account manager (vendor-account): Monthly service report to Calder Quay Hotel. July / August: rooms serviced 5,812 / 5,990; rooms released by 15:00 98% / 97%; self-audit quality score 97% / 97%; average attendants per shift 21 / 22; two attendant absences in August covered by agency staff. Report note: 'The client notified no service failures in either month. Several attendants reported very warm conditions on floors 6-8 during mid-August and were given extra breaks.'
26	C2 [stage S1] Front-office staffing rotas and overtime, June-August 2026 - Hotel workforce management system (system-record): Front-office rota summary. Headcount: June 18.0 FTE, July 18.5, August 18.0. Overtime hours: June 112, July 96, August 104. In July, two new agents completed kiosk and desk training. No peak-hour shifts went unfilled in July or August. A duty manager was on the rota every night in August.
27	C3 [stage S1] Self-check-in kiosk supplier support tickets, June-September 2026 - Kiosk supplier service desk (vendor-account): Support log for Calder Quay. 11 tickets since go-live on 23 June: 8 between 23 June and 6 July (key-card encoder calibration, receipt printer jams), 2 later in July (screen freeze, fixed by restart), 1 in August (receipt paper sensor). Kiosk availability: July 99.1%, August 99.6%. No tickets open at 31 August.
28	C4 [stage S1] Public review-site ratings and comments, July-August 2026 - Guest relations extract from public review sites (external-data): July: 58 reviews, average 4.4/5. August: 63 reviews, average 4.1/5. August reviews mentioning heat, air conditioning or stuffy rooms: 19 (July: 0). Mentioning cleanliness or dust: 2 (July: 3). One of these is the 'tired and dusty' review, which also says the room was 'like an oven'. Mentioning check-in: 3 positive, 1 negative. Mentioning price: 3 (July: 2).
29	C5 [stage S1] Survey vendor methodology statement, 2026 - Pellmore Insights client services (vendor-account): Invitations go out 24 hours after checkout to every stay with a valid email address; there is no sampling. Questionnaire version Q7 has been in use since January 2025 with no changes to wording, scale or order. Response rates: June 31%, July 31%, August 30%. The invitation template, timing and reminder schedule have not changed in 2026.
30	C6 [stage S1] Building management system corridor temperature trends, August 2026 - Building management system export (telemetry): Hourly averages from floor 6-8 corridor sensors. 1-3 Aug: 21.8-22.6 C. 4 Aug: rising from 16:00. 6-18 Aug: daytime 27.4-30.2 C, overnight 25.9-27.1 C. 19 Aug: falls from 28.6 C at 14:00 to 22.9 C at 22:00. 20-31 Aug: 21.7-22.8 C. Floor 1-5 corridor sensors stayed at 21.5-23.0 C all through August.
31	C7 [stage S1] Guest compensation and room-move ledger, August 2026 - Finance and front office (financial-record): Guest recovery ledger, August. Room moves from floors 6-8 to floors 1-5: 14 (limited by 91% occupancy). Portable cooling units hired: 12, EUR 1,150. Goodwill credits issued at checkout, with a written apology, to all floor 6-8 stays checking out 5-20 August: 517 stays, about EUR 45,750 in total (half of one night's rate each). Credits for all other causes in August: EUR 640 (July: EUR 710).
32	C8 [stage S1] Competitive-set guest satisfaction benchmark, June-August 2026 - Merrowby hotel association shared survey programme (external-data): Benchmark across five comparable four-star hotels in Merrowby (anonymised). Average overall guest satisfaction: June 8.4, July 8.4, August 8.3. None of the participating hotels reported a building-systems outage in August. The association does not publish individual hotels' pricing or rate changes.
33	C9 [stage S1] Municipal weather station daily records, August 2026 - Merrowby municipal weather station (external-data): Daily maximum temperatures: 1-5 Aug 24-27 C; 6-17 Aug 31-35 C (heat advisory 8-16 Aug); 18-31 Aug 23-28 C. The August mean maximum was 29.6 C, against a ten-year August average of 26.1 C.
34	C10 [stage S1] Housekeeping staff pulse survey, August 2026 - Anonymous pulse survey of Orrin attendants and in-house supervisors (anonymous-staff-survey): 27 responses from 41 invited. 'I have the supplies I need': 85% agree. 'My room quota is manageable': 52% agree (May, under Linthwaite: 49%). 'I am proud of the standard of rooms I hand over': 81% agree. Free-text themes: heat on the upper floors in August (9 mentions), uniform sizing (4), timing of linen deliveries (3).
35	C11 [stage S1] Rate change record and occupancy report, July-August 2026 - Revenue management system (system-record): BAR increase: +6% on all room types from 1 August (budgeted in November 2025). Average daily rate: July EUR 171, August EUR 177 (August 2025: EUR 166). Occupancy: July 88%, August 91% (August 2025: 90%). August channel mix: direct 38%, online agencies 47%, corporate 15% (July: 37 / 48 / 15). The revenue system holds no guest-satisfaction data.
36	C12 [stage S1] Finance memo on engineering maintenance deferrals, April 2026 - Director of Finance to General Manager (document): Memo, 14 April 2026: 'To meet the Q2 cost target we are moving the following engineering items to Q3: annual preventive service on chillers CH-1 and CH-2 (EUR 6,800 combined, including contactor and relay inspection and the recommended spares kit); cooling-tower descale (EUR 2,100); lobby carpet replacement (EUR 14,000). Engineering notes that the chiller service has been overdue since January. We will revisit this at the July forecast.'
37	C13 [stage S1] Food and beverage outlet satisfaction scores, July-August 2026 - Pellmore Insights F&B module (system-record): Breakfast restaurant: July 8.3, August 8.3. Lobby bar: July 8.1, August 8.2. Room service: July 7.9, August 7.6; August comments mention 'slow' (5) and 'ice delivery' (3). Each outlet gets 90-210 responses a month.
38	C14 [stage S1] Loyalty-member complaint emails, August 2026 - Loyalty desk inbox (customer-account): 12 complaint emails in August. 9 came from guests on floors 6-8 about room heat between 5 and 18 August; three of them asked why they had not been moved. 1 was about the new rate ('paid more for the same room'). 1 was about late-night noise from a wedding party. 1 was about a duplicated card charge. July had 5 complaint emails, none about temperature.
39	C15 [stage S1] Interview with the Chief Engineer, 8 September 2026 - Interview notes, Ruth Abernathy-Sole, Chief Engineer (manager-account): 'The contactor is a wear part. The annual service checks it, and the kit we normally buy with the service includes a spare. Without the service we had no spare, so we waited eleven working days for one. CH-1 is the same model and age as CH-2, and its service is overdue too. I can't say CH-1 will fail, but if it does during a hot spell, floors 1-5 go the same way. Apart from that, the units are in reasonable shape.'
40	CANDIDATES
41	H1: A failure of in-room cooling during August caused the drop in the overall score.
42	H2: Problems with check-in after the front-desk system change caused the drop in the overall score.
43	H3: A decline in housekeeping quality after the contractor change caused the drop in the overall score.
44	H4: A change in how the guest survey was administered produced the drop in the overall score.
45	H5: The 1 August room-rate increase contributed to the drop in the overall score.
46	R1: CH-2 chiller outage, 4-19 August -> Lower August ratings from guests on floors 6-8 (causes)
47	R2: Self-check-in kiosk go-live, 23 June -> Lower August overall score (causes)
48	R3: 6% room-rate increase, 1 August -> Lower August value-for-money ratings (causes)
49	R4: Housekeeping contractor change, 1 July -> Lower cleanliness ratings (causes)
50	A1: Reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and set a written guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages.
51	A2: Serve notice on the Orrin Facility Group housekeeping contract before the 1 October renewal window.
52	A3: Reverse the 1 August room-rate increase to restore value-for-money ratings.
53	A4: Send an apology and a return-stay offer to guests who stayed on floors 6-8 during the cooling outage.
54	A5: Exclude the August floor 6-8 survey responses from the reported GSS as an outlier month.

answers.justification: The drop is limited to floors 6-8 and to room comfort (E2). Those floors' scores fall on 5-20 Aug and recover once CH-2 is fixed (E4, E3, C6), heat accounts for 56 of 74 negative comments (E4), and room-temperature complaints at the desk went from 1 to 24 (E5).
Check-in scores are flat (E2), kiosk complaints and comments slightly fell (E4, E5), queues got shorter (E5), kiosk availability was 99.6% (C3), and front-office staffing was stable (C2).
Cleanliness scores are steady on both floor blocks (E2), inspection pass rates are 95-96% (E5), and cleanliness comments did not rise (E4, C4); the 'dusty' review also complained of heat (C4).
The questionnaire, invitation method, timing and response rates did not change (E2, C5), and floors 1-5 were stable over the same period (E2, E4).

On floors 1-5, value for money fell 0.3 while the overall score fell only 0.1, which is within normal variation (E2). The Revenue Manager cannot separate the rate rise from the usual August seasonal dip (E6, C11), so any contribution is unestablished.
The timing matches (E3, C6, E4), the mechanism is clear (chiller trip leading to 26.5-29 C rooms, E3), floors 1-5 act as a control group (E2), and scores recovered after the repair (E4).
The kiosks went live in June but July's score was 8.6, check-in scores and complaints did not change (E2, E5), and the kiosks worked reliably (C3).
The rate rise came at the same time as the drop in value scores (E2, C11), but the usual seasonal August dip (E6) is a confounder that has not been ruled out.
Cleanliness ratings did not fall after the contractor changed (8.7 to 8.7 on floors 1-5, 8.7 to 8.6 on floors 6-8, E2), inspection pass rates held (E5), and cleanliness comments were flat (E4).
The deferred preventive service and the missing spare part caused the 11-day outage (E3, C12, C15), and CH-1 is the same model, the same age and also overdue (C15).
No evidence shows that Orrin's quality declined (E2, E5, C1, C10), so serving notice would punish the wrong party for an engineering failure.
There is no evidence yet that the rate rise caused the value drop rather than the seasonal dip (E6, C11), and rates can be changed at any time, so there is no rush (E6).
All 517 affected stays already received a written apology and a half-night credit (E5, C7), so another apology with a return-stay offer is reasonable but adds less than A1.
The floor 6-8 responses are valid feedback from a real failure (E2, E4, C5), so leaving them out of a bonus-linked score would hide information.
The evidence pins the cause on the CH-2 outage with deferred maintenance behind it (E2-E4, C6, C12, C15), which is enough to commit to A1.
